title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
blurb: First published in 1936, Dale Carnegie's classic grew out of the courses he taught adults on speaking and dealing with people. His core belief is simple: people are driven by emotion and pride far more than logic, and almost everyone deeply wants to feel important. The book is organised into practical principles. It shows how to handle people without stirring up resentment, how to make others genuinely like you, how to win people to your way of thinking without arguing, and how to change behaviour without giving offence. Carnegie illustrates each idea with stories of business leaders, historical figures and his own students. Above all, he insists these methods only work when they are sincere. Flattery and manipulation backfire. Real curiosity, appreciation and respect for the other person's point of view are what open doors.

lessons.b: Criticism makes people defensive and resentful, so it almost never changes behaviour. Understanding them works far better.
issues: scene 6: Below the 'Why?' box and the three check circles there are two disconnected curved strokes. They read as a broken drawing, perhaps an unfinished face or open hands, and do not clearly illustrate 'reasons that make sense to them'. (fix: Replace the two loose arcs with a clear element, such as a simple person figure holding the checkmarks or a thought bubble containing them. Otherwise remove the arcs so the 'Why?' box, checks and label stand on their own.)

lessons.b: The deepest human hunger is to feel appreciated, so honest and sincere appreciation is one of the most powerful tools you have.
To move someone to act, stop talking about what you want and show them how it gets them what they want.
